episodes.201189: Several afternoons of thunderstorm activity occurred during the fourth week of May, with hail and wind damage being reported around Central Alabama over the course of four days. In addition, heavy rainfall on May 27 resulted in several impassable roadways along Terrapin Creek in Cherokee County.
episodes.201539: A strong supercell thunderstorm tracked south-southeast across far northeast Weld, southwest Logan and northwest Washington Counties. The storms produced large hail, up to 3 inches in diameter and also three tornadoes across Logan and Washington Counties during the afternoon hours of May 23rd, including one EF-2 and one EF-1. Most of the observed damage was snapped power poles and trees. One single family residence sustained EF-1 damage, but there were no injuries reported. This supercell also produced a swath of golf ball to baseball sized hail, with one ICECHIP report of over 3 inch diameter hail in northern Washington county.
episodes.201540: Two supercell thunderstorms tracked eastward across the western part of Elbert County during the afternoon of May 24th.
episodes.201640: Severe thunderstorm watch for Laramie County and most of the Nebraska Panhandle.
episodes.201643: Isolated wind gust reported in Scottsbluff causing some roof damage to KNEB.
episodes.202151: Clusters of storms developed in the late evening in northeast Colorado. After exiting Colorado, the storms developed into a marginal MCS. It tracked eastward, reaching severe thresholds just before exiting the CWA.
episodes.202204: On the afternoon of the 23rd, a few low precipitation supercells form in eastern Colorado and proceeded to the east, before turning to the southeast. As these storms turned to the southeast, they quickly intensified and began producing hail up to 2.75 inches. A brief tornado was also reported south of Kit Carson.
episodes.202231: A passing shortwave interacting with a dryline resulted in scattered thunderstorm development over the central and eastern Permian Basin and Trans-Pecos region of West Texas during the afternoon of May 24th. These thunderstorms produced damaging winds/microbursts and quarter size hail before they moved to the northeast of the area overnight.
episodes.202437: The approximately 36-hour period, beginning during the initial hours of the 24th, featured three unique severe convective episodes across the WFO Norman Forecast Area. The initial round, triggered by moist isentropic ascent, featured scattered organized thunderstorms, including a few supercell thunderstorms. This activity produced primarily reports of large hail. However, localized storm-scale interactions across Cleveland, Pottawatomie, and Pontotoc Counties resulted in concentrated corridor of thunderstorm wind damage, as well as a tornado near Vanoss, OK, in Pontotoc County. During the same general time frame, a separate organized line of thunderstorms moved from far southern Kansas into north-central Oklahoma producing a few observed severe-caliber wind gusts. ||Following the morning activity, dry and pleasant conditions occurred for much of the day on the 24th. However, by near-sunset, a destabilizing boundary layer near and south of a warm front across western and southern Oklahoma fostered the development of a few briefly intense thunderstorms. Finally, a progressive and high-intensity wake low and heat burst event evolved from portions of western-north Texas into central Oklahoma during the late evening of the 24th into the 25th. This event, tied to decaying severe convection from across central Texas, featured strong and occasionally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202521: Multiple thunderstorms across east central Florida produced severe hail, some of which was large.
episodes.202550: Thunderstorms developed in eastern Wyoming and the western Nebraska Panhandle in the vicinity of a surface trough mid afternoon on May 23rd. This activity tracked east into Sheridan County where it produced golf ball sized hail. The storm then weakened as it tracked east into the Sandhills.
episodes.202605: Clusters of thunderstorms developed along the I-20 corridor in northern Louisiana and Mississippi midday on May 24th. These storms congealed into a weak Mesoscale Convective System. The leading edge cold pool pulled is southeastward into southern Mississippi and produced a severe thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.202615: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms occurred from Friday, May 23 through Tuesday, May 27, 2025. Total Rainfall amounts ranged between 2-5 inches, with localized amounts up to 8.6 inches.
episodes.202712: A decaying mesoscale convective system entered the region during the overnight hours, bringing showers and thunderstorms across the Mid-South. A weakening shortwave and just enough instability supported a rogue severe storm, which produced wind damage across eastern Arkansas.
episodes.202846: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 24th, as the low level jet increased lift over a frontal boundary that stretched across the area. Strong elevated instability and wind shear resulted in some of the storms becoming supercells, which produced large hail up to baseball size. An organized line of severe thunderstorms that developed over southwestern Kansas during the late evening of the 23rd, moved into portions of eastern Oklahoma during the morning of the 24th. These thunderstorms produced widespread damaging wind gusts.
episodes.202877: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of western Kansas during the evening hours of May 23rd. These thunderstorms merged into a line and moved southeast across portions central, south central, and southeast Kansas during the morning hours of May 24th. Additional thunderstorms developed in advance of the line of thunderstorms from northeast Reno County into Sedgwick and Butler counties. Fortunately, severe weather and damage was very limited with only two reports of severe criteria wind gusts being reported at the Wellington Airport and in Caney.
episodes.203036: In the evening of the 24th, two fairly weak storms collided in western Decatur county and briefly produced hail up to 1 inch.
episodes.203145: Upper level ridging was centered over Northern Old Mexico and much of Texas during the morning of May 24th, resulting in a northwesterly flow aloft farther north across much of Oklahoma and Arkansas. A weak shortwave trough embedded in the northwest flow resulted in surface low development along the dryline in West Texas, with large scale forcing ahead of this trough resulting in the development of a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) over Western and Central Oklahoma during the early morning hours. A southerly low level jet, typical for this time of year in this flow pattern, sustained this thunderstorm complex as it shifted east-southeast into Southeast Oklahoma after daybreak, which moved across Northern McCurtain County before weakening as it moved into Western Arkansas. As a result, damaging winds downed multiple trees near the Bethel community before exiting the county into Polk County Arkansas.
episodes.203557: An upper level disturbance moving across the state atop moist southerly low-level flow enabled the development of thunderstorms that produced severe hail near Lehigh Acres in Lee County.
episodes.203575: Ample moisture, a decaying surface boundary, and a disturbance at the mid to upper levels of the atmosphere supported the development of strong to severe thunderstorms over southern Florida in the afternoon and evening hours of May 23, 2025.
episodes.203576: Thunderstorms develop over portions of the Lake Okeechobee region and inland southern Florida as the Atlantic and Gulf sea breezes collided in the later afternoon and early evening.
episodes.203720: Ample moisture, a decaying surface boundary, and a disturbance at the mid to upper levels of the atmosphere supported the development of strong to severe thunderstorms over southern Florida in the afternoon and evening hours of May 23, 2025.
episodes.204264: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across southeast Arkansas and caused wind damage.
episodes.204267: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across Mississippi with hail and damaging winds.
episodes.204268: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across northeast Louisiana with hail and damaging winds.
episodes.204269: A broad shortwave pushed over the region, bringing increased shear and moisture, allowing for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop across eastern Colorado, one of which pushed into Kiowa County.
episodes.204270: A broad shortwave pushed over the region, bringing increased shear and moisture and upslope along the Palmer Divide, allowing for severe storms to develop, along with a supercell.
episodes.204334: River flooding was observed along the Cache, Black, and Fourche LaFave Rivers.
episodes.204569: Rounds of showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front over northern Alabama ahead of an approaching cold front during the late  morning and afternoon hours.  Tragically, a boater on Lake Guntersville was struck by lightning while fishing and was seriously injured.
episodes.204757: Heavy rains brought isolated flash flooding to portions of Arkansas.
